title: User Journey & Persona Analysis
insights:
USER JOURNEY ANALYSIS FOR BUS TICKET BOOKING APP

The analysis is based on a dataset containing 14,952 events from 381 users, covering the period from November 27, 2025, to February 22, 2026. A total of 252 users were analyzed for their journey through the app.

USER TYPE BREAKDOWN

Based on the journey statistics:

  • Browsers: 2 users (0.79%)
  • Shoppers: 1 user (0.40%)
  • Attempters: 0 users (0.00%)
  • Bookers: 0 users (0.00%)

The funnel shape indicates a significant drop-off from Browsers to Shoppers, suggesting that while users are interested in searching for tickets, very few are progressing to seat selection and payment initiation. This indicates low intent to complete the booking process.

FRICTION IMPACT

No users faced payment failures or app errors during their journey. This indicates that friction related to payment processing is not currently a churn driver in this dataset.

POWER USERS VS CASUALS

Given the statistics, a "high-intent" user can be defined as someone who not only searches for tickets but also selects a seat and initiates payment. In this dataset, there are no users who have reached the payment initiation stage, highlighting a lack of high-intent users.

PERSONALIZATION SUGGESTIONS FOR BROWSERS

To convert Browsers into Shoppers, consider the following strategies:

  • Enhanced Seat Selection Experience: Implement features that allow Browsers to visualize available seats better, such as a dynamic seating chart or highlighting popular seats based on user preferences.
  • Incentives for Seat Selection: Offer limited-time discounts or rewards for users who select a seat within a specific timeframe after searching, encouraging them to take the next step in the booking process.
